stories.image_caption: Phu Quoc barracuda cakes in the article introduce how to make and local dishes.

sections.heading: Cong is located at the time of the fish
sections.body: Fresh barracuda after being preliminarily processed is ground or crushed, followed by the seasoning stage with shallots, peppercorns and basic spices. The patty maker must use his hands to whisk evenly so that the fish meat mixture becomes flexible, increasing structural cohesion before forming into bite-sized patties. Although the press once praised a barracuda cake recipe using the famous Phu Quoc skull pepper, in fact, the ratio of spice mixing, light saltiness and fish processing techniques always vary depending on the secrets of each chef. Understand that the richness of flavors is what makes it attractive, don't be in a hurry to attribute a certain seasoning recipe to the common standard for all barracuda cakes on the island.

sections.heading: Soft steamed pork rolls, fragrant fried pork rolls
sections.body: If steamed fish cakes score points for their soft texture and ability to preserve the sweet flavor of fish meat, the fried fish cake version captivates diners with its golden outer shell, emitting an extremely stimulating aroma. These barracuda cakes are very versatile, can be served with vermicelli, soup cakes, or simply eaten with a bowl of hot white rice. When you buy fish cakes as a gift, don't forget to ask the seller carefully about the expiration date as well as the safest storage method, especially on hot days when you have to travel long distances.

sections.heading: If you want the right barracuda fish, just ask
sections.body: It should be known that not all fish cakes sold in Phu Quoc are made from barracua meat. When ordering, you should actively ask the owner what kind of fish the patties you are about to eat are made from and what processing methods go through. For those who have a history of allergies to certain types of marine fish, a thorough inspection of the patties, broth to cups of dipping sauce is a step not to be missed; because the kitchen environment of the restaurant can very well process many types of seafood at the same time.

stories.title: Phu Quoc snails: shaggy shell, crispy meat
stories.dek: Identified by the tassel shell with shaggy sharp tabs, spiny snails compensate with extremely crunchy meat. The restaurant likes to grill onion fat, the restaurant likes to boil ethereal lemongrass; to find out what the shop has snails today and how much it sells for, you need to ask the waiter directly.
stories.intro: Mixed with countless types of fresh seafood in the basket, prickly snails always know how to catch the eyes of diners thanks to their shaggy outer shell, tassels of sharp thorns. In contrast to that somewhat fierce appearance, the snail meat inside brings an explosive taste experience with a rough crunchyness, whether it is grilled or boiled with lemongrass dipped in salt and pepper and lemongrass, it is excellent. Spiny snails are a constant name in articles praising Phu Quoc cuisine, but the truth is that this type of snail is not always available in a glass tank waiting for you to order at any restaurant.

sections.heading: Looking at the shell knows the folk name
sections.body: The name "spiny snails", or sometimes more aphocmatically called "cactus snails", comes from the shape of their outer shell. However, the popular name written on the bar menu is still not enough for scientists to accurately identify which species of snail this is in the biological classification system. If you're really interested in the origin of the catch or the type of snail in detail, ask the restaurant directly instead of speculating on your own based on a familiar name.

sections.heading: Grilled or boiled, it needs to be medium heat
sections.body: Grilled snails with onion fat exude a pleasant aroma, the snail meat is firm and rich in spices; while the boiled snail version helps diners fully feel the original sweetness of seafood. Many talented chefs also create other attractive processing methods such as stir-fried snails with tamarind or steamed lemongrass. On the first time you touch the alley with prickly snails, you can ask the waiter for instructions on how to get the snail meat, and remember to taste an original piece before dipping it into a cup of dipping sauce; because sometimes the restaurant's seafood dipping sauce is prepared with a rather harsh taste.

sections.heading: Ask the price before calling
sections.body: Many old food articles have mentioned the price and scarcity of snails at the time of publication, but you should definitely not use those "antique" numbers to impose on your trip today. Be tactful and ask the staff what kind of snails the restaurant is currently selling, whether the billing is by the plate or the scale, and whether the listed price includes processing costs. In particular, passengers with a history of allergies to mollusks need to ask for the composition of the dipping sauce cup and confirm whether the kitchen utensils are cleaned separately to reduce the risk.

stories.title: Grilled abalone in Phu Quoc: embers, onion fat, green salt and pepper
stories.dek: Fresh abalone sizzling on the charcoal grill, blending with the greasy taste of onion fat or the spicy richness of green salt and pepper. However, the way to marinate and quantify the meal always varies between restaurants.
stories.intro: Grilled abalone is always in a solemn position on the list of premium seafood dishes that must be tried when coming to Phu Quoc, often juggled with greasy onion fat or spicy green salt and pepper. Some restaurants marinate abalone with esoteric spices and then bring it to the charcoal grill, while others focus on grilling techniques so that the meat is just cooked to serve as a launching pad for sublimated dipping sauces and spices. Therefore, even if you call the same name, the plate of grilled abalone served in front of you may not have the same seasoning style as the restaurant you ate yesterday.

sections.heading: Charcoal grilling, spices depending on the stove
sections.body: Mainstream information sites used to depict the image of abalone being grilled sizzling over a charcoal fire, served with onion fat drizzled on top or dipped in a cup of green pepper salt is a specialty of the island. Meanwhile, other reputable culinary guides describe the recipe of marinating the abalone meat soaked in the abalone meat before being grilled browned and fragrant, which is "unique". These are merely slices of reality, but there is no general law governing the way grilled abalone is prepared by all restaurants. To have a satisfactory meal, when ordering, you should actively ask the waiter what kind of spices the abalone is marinated, whether the onion fat is pre-sprinkled or reserved, and whether the restaurant has green salt and pepper available for you to change the taste.

sections.heading: The crispy toughness is in the meat
sections.body: According to gourmet reviews, the meat texture of a standard grilled abalone must converge with enough moderate chewiness and interesting crispiness. The trick for you is to slowly chew a piece of original abalone meat before adding any sauce; this is the most subtle way for you to judge how far the chef's seasoning skills have reached. In the case of onion fat or dipping sauce served separately in small cups, diners have the full right to regulate the amount of spices served with it, avoiding the strong flavor of the sauce from overpowering the natural sweetness of the abalone meat.

sections.heading: Ask for portions and calculations
sections.body: The size of each abalone, the number of servings in a serving, and the processing technique can vary greatly from restaurant to restaurant. To avoid surprises about the bill, make it a habit to ask whether the restaurant is charging the price of abalone by each fish, by fixed plate, or by weight before deciding to order. In addition, diners with seafood allergies must immediately inform the waiter, and ask carefully about the marinated spices, dipping sauce ingredients, and whether the restaurant shares the grill with other seafood.

stories.title: Mango salad with snails: the crunchy sour of mangoes, the chewiness of snails
stories.dek: The snail meat is boiled until cooked, thinly sliced and then artfully mixed with minced green mango and sweet and sour fish sauce. The presence of spinach, onion, roasted peanuts or fried onions will flexibly change depending on the variation of each kitchen.
stories.intro: In addition to the familiar herring salad and barracuda salad, the food map of Phu Quoc also records the presence of an equally excellent delicacy: snail mango salad. After being boiled, the snail meat core will be skillfully sliced into thin slices by the chefs, then mixed with shredded green mango. The feeling of biting into the teeth of the chewy, rough snail mixed with the crispy and sour taste of green mango is indescribable; meanwhile, the sweet and sour fish sauce mixed with the herbs acts as a "glue" that connects the layers of flavor together perfectly. Depending on the style of each restaurant, the salad plate can be dotted with thinly sliced onions, warm strips of ginger, fragrant fried onions or crispy roasted peanuts.
stories.image_alt: Snail mango salad in the introduction of Phu Quoc specialties
stories.image_caption: Snail mango salad according to the introduction of Phu Quoc cuisine; the photo is not used to identify which restaurant is serving.

sections.heading: Boiled snails before slicing
sections.body: According to a recorded traditional preparation recipe, whole fresh snails will be boiled, taken out to drain, then cut into very thin slices with a sharp knife; combined with fresh green mango grated into small fibers to mix salad. Slicing the snail meat thin enough not only helps the snail to soak up the salad but also preserves the characteristic crunchy and crunchy taste. It should be remembered that the secret to preparing snails and the thin thickness of the slices is the "best trick" for each chef to affirm his or her own style.

sections.heading: Mixed water that combines sour taste with sea taste
sections.body: If green mango plays the role of a "conductor" that brings a mild sour taste and crunch, the mixed fish sauce is subtly adjusted to favor a mild sweet and sour aftertaste, often with the participation of minced garlic and fresh chili peppers to add spiciness. Depending on the restaurant's esoteric recipe, auxiliary ingredients such as spinach, onion, fresh ginger or fried onions will be increased differently; some places even favor adding roasted and pounded peanuts to enhance the fatty taste of the dish. Therefore, you should not assume that every plate of mango salad served on the table must comply with a single accompanying ingredient.

sections.heading: Ask the ingredient before calling
sections.body: In some unique variations, the recipe for snail salad also has the "participation" of slices of fatty boiled pork belly, roasted peanuts or served with crispy grilled rice paper. If you are the type of person who is allergic to seafood, peanuts or fish, do not hesitate to immediately inform the service staff, and at the same time ask carefully about the ingredients of fish sauce, salad mix recipe as well as the use of processing tools in the kitchen. Although snail mango salad is widely promoted as a Phu Quoc specialty, in fact, not every restaurant has a fresh source of ingredients available to serve this dish every day.
